summary: The repository contains two parallel implementations of an 'eShop' Catalog web application: a legacy ASP.NET MVC 5 / Web API 2 application (src/eShopLegacyMVC) targeting classic .NET Framework, and a strangler-fig / ported ASP.NET Core 2.2 application (eShopPorted) targeting net461 via Microsoft.NET.Sdk.Web. Both share a nearly identical layered design: MVC controllers, Web API controllers, an ICatalogService abstraction with a real EF-backed CatalogService and a CatalogServiceMock, and Catalog domain models (CatalogItem, CatalogBrand, CatalogType) persisted through a CatalogDBContext (EF6 in the legacy app, EF Core 2.2.6 in the ported app). A shared eShopLegacy.Utilities library provides binary serialization used by both apps' Files/Brands API controllers. Autofac provides dependency injection in both versions via near-duplicate ApplicationModule classes, and log4net provides logging. The legacy app additionally wires Application Insights telemetry, bundling/optimization, and classic Global.asax/App_Start startup, while the ported app uses Startup.cs/Program.cs (Kestrel/IWebHostBuilder) and EF Core Migrations with a code-first model snapshot. A PowerShell script (Convert-ToPackageReference.ps1) suggests active migration tooling from packages.config to PackageReference format, reinforcing that this is a migration-in-progress repository rather than a single coherent architecture.
architectural_styles: Strangler-fig / parallel migration pattern (legacy ASP.NET MVC & WebAPI alongside ported ASP.NET Core equivalent)
Repository/Service abstraction via ICatalogService with interchangeable real and mock implementations
Code-first ORM data access (Entity Framework 6 / EF Core)

components.name: eShopLegacyMVC Web Application

components.name: eShopPorted Web Application
components.responsibility: Ported/modernized web front-end and REST API surface for catalog browsing/management, hosted via Kestrel/IWebHostBuilder with Startup.cs configuration.

components.name: eShopLegacy.Utilities
components.responsibility: Provides cross-cutting binary serialization/deserialization helpers reused by both the legacy and ported Web API file/brand endpoints.

components.name: Catalog MVC Controllers
components.responsibility: Handles browser-facing CRUD requests (Index/Create/Edit/Delete/Details) for catalog items, present in duplicate legacy and ported forms.

components.name: Catalog Web API Controllers
components.responsibility: Exposes brand, file, and catalog data over HTTP APIs (WebApi/BrandsController, WebApi/FilesController, Api/CatalogController, PicController) in both legacy WebAPI2 and ported ASP.NET Core Mvc styles.

components.name: Catalog Service Layer (legacy)
components.responsibility: Implements ICatalogService for the legacy app, with a real EF6-backed CatalogService and an in-memory CatalogServiceMock alternative selected presumably by configuration.

components.name: Catalog Service Layer (ported)
components.responsibility: Implements ICatalogService for the ported app, with a real EF Core-backed CatalogService and an in-memory CatalogServiceMock; appsettings.json exposes a UseMockData flag suggesting runtime toggling.

components.name: Catalog Domain Models (legacy)
components.responsibility: Defines CatalogItem, CatalogBrand, CatalogType entities and the PaginatedItemsViewModel used across legacy controllers, services, and views.

components.name: Catalog Domain Models (ported)
components.responsibility: Defines CatalogItem, CatalogBrand, CatalogType entities and Fluent API configuration classes (CatalogBrandConfig/CatalogTypeConfig/CatalogItemConfig) for the ported EF Core context.

components.name: CatalogDBContext (legacy/EF6)
components.responsibility: Entity Framework 6 DbContext configuring catalog entities via DbModelBuilder, seeded via CatalogDBInitializer, and relying on a custom HiLo ID generator with raw SQL sequence queries.

components.name: CatalogDBContext (ported/EF Core)
components.responsibility: EF Core 2.2 DbContext applying IEntityTypeConfiguration classes from the assembly and seeding via HasData/PreconfiguredData; supports EF Core Migrations.

components.name: Autofac DI Modules
components.responsibility: Registers services (ICatalogService implementations) and controllers with Autofac's ContainerBuilder in both legacy (Global.asax RegisterContainer) and ported (Startup.ConfigureServices) hosting models.

components.name: Preconfigured/Seed Data
components.responsibility: Supplies hardcoded catalog brand/type/item seed data used by both DB initializers/migrations to populate a fresh database.

components.name: Migration Tooling Script
components.responsibility: PowerShell script (Convert-ToPackageReference.ps1) that converts legacy packages.config-based NuGet references to PackageReference format, indicating in-progress project modernization tooling.

risks.title: Duplicate parallel codebases increase maintenance and divergence risk
risks.description: The repository contains two nearly complete, independently evolving implementations of the same Catalog application (src/eShopLegacyMVC and eShopPorted) with duplicated controllers, services, models, and DI modules. Any bug fix or feature must be manually ported to both, and it's unclear which is authoritative, increasing risk of behavioral drift during the migration window.

evidence.observation: Nearly identical controller logic exists in eShopPorted/Controllers/CatalogController.cs
Duplicated service layer structurally mirrors src/eShopLegacyMVC/Services/CatalogService.cs

risks.title: Use of BinaryFormatter-based serialization is insecure and deprecated
risks.description: The shared eShopLegacy.Utilities.Serializing class uses binary serialization (implied by SerializeBinary/DeserializeBinary over Stream) to transmit DTOs via Web API endpoints in both apps. BinaryFormatter-style serialization is known to be vulnerable to deserialization attacks and is deprecated/removed in modern .NET, posing both a security and forward-compatibility risk during modernization.

evidence.observation: Serializing.SerializeBinary/DeserializeBinary operate on System.IO.Stream, consistent with BinaryFormatter usage patterns.
FilesController.Index serializes brand DTOs via Serializing.SerializeBinary and returns raw bytes over HTTP.

risks.title: Raw SQL sequence queries bypass ORM abstraction for ID generation
risks.description: CatalogItemHiLoGenerator executes a raw 'SELECT NEXT VALUE FOR catalog_hilo' SQL query directly against the DbContext.Database in the legacy app, coupling business logic tightly to specific SQL Server sequence objects and bypassing EF's abstraction layer, which complicates database portability and safe migration to EF Core.

evidence.observation: Uses db.Database.SqlQuery<Int64>("SELECT NEXT VALUE FOR catalog_hilo;") for custom HiLo ID generation.
Raw SQL script defines the catalog_hilo sequence object outside of EF Code First migrations.

risks.title: Legacy .NET Framework dependency and outdated NuGet packages
risks.description: The legacy project targets classic ASP.NET MVC5/WebAPI2 on .NET Framework with EntityFramework, Microsoft.AspNet.WebApi, and other framework-era packages that are out of long-term support, indicating this component needs a full framework upgrade path beyond the partial porting already attempted.

evidence.observation: References legacy packages such as Microsoft.AspNet.Mvc, Microsoft.AspNet.WebApi, EntityFramework, and Microsoft.AspNet.Razor.
Presence of packages.config indicates legacy NuGet package management style predating PackageReference.

risks.title: Ported project still targets net461 despite using ASP.NET Core SDK
risks.description: eShopPorted.csproj uses Microsoft.NET.Sdk.Web but targets framework net461 rather than a modern .NET (Core/5+) TFM, meaning the 'ported' application has not fully left the .NET Framework runtime, undermining the goal of true modernization.

evidence.observation: Graph metadata shows framework_net461 associated with eShopPorted.csproj alongside sdk_microsoft_net_sdk_web.

risks.title: Mock vs real service selection logic is implicit and undocumented
risks.description: Both codebases implement CatalogServiceMock alongside the real CatalogService, and eShopPorted/appsettings.json exposes a 'UseMockData' flag, but the wiring/branching logic that decides which implementation is registered is not evident from the DI modules alone, risking inconsistent behavior between environments if misconfigured.

evidence.observation: Contains "UseMockData": "true" and "UseCustomizationData": "true" flags controlling seed/mock behavior.
Autofac module presumably registers either CatalogService or CatalogServiceMock, but the conditional logic is not directly visible in supplied evidence.

risks.title: Duplicated seed/preconfigured data increases risk of data drift between environments
risks.description: Both the legacy CatalogDBInitializer/PreconfiguredData and the ported EF Core PreconfiguredData/Config classes hardcode the same catalog seed data independently, so any change to reference data must be manually synchronized across two codebases and seeding mechanisms (custom initializer vs EF Core HasData/migrations).

evidence.observation: Legacy static seed data provider used by CatalogDBInitializer.Seed().
Ported static seed data provider used by CatalogBrandConfig/CatalogTypeConfig/CatalogItemConfig via HasData().

risks.title: Telemetry and monitoring not yet ported
risks.description: Application Insights configuration and dependency collection exist only in the legacy project (ApplicationInsights.config, multiple Microsoft.ApplicationInsights.* NuGet packages) with no equivalent observability stack evidenced in the ported ASP.NET Core project, creating an observability gap post-migration.

evidence.observation: Dedicated Application Insights configuration file present only under src/eShopLegacyMVC.
References numerous Microsoft.ApplicationInsights.* packages not present in eShopPorted.csproj dependency list.
